claim:
Let \(ABC\) be a nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with side lengths \(a=BC\), \(b=CA\), \(c=AB\), area \(\Delta\), and \(S=a^2+b^2+c^2\). Let \(K\) be its symmedian (Lemoine) point. For arbitrary \(X\in BC\), \(Y\in CA\), and \(Z\in AB\), let \(M\) be the centroid of \(XYZ\), and let \(D_a,D_b,D_c\) be the perpendicular feet from \(M\) to the lines \(BC,CA,AB\). If \(n_a,n_b,n_c\) are consistently oriented unit normals to those three sidelines, then
\[
XY^2+YZ^2+ZX^2=\frac{12\Delta^2}{S}+3\sum_{i\in\{a,b,c\}}\bigl(n_i\cdot(M-K)\bigr)^2+3\bigl(D_aX^2+D_bY^2+D_cZ^2\bigr).
\]
Consequently, among all triangles \(XYZ\) inscribed in \(ABC\), the minimum of \(XY^2+YZ^2+ZX^2\) is exactly \(12\Delta^2/S\), attained uniquely by the pedal triangle of \(K\).
scientific_limitations: The classical Lemoine-pedal optimizer is prior work; the claim concerns the exact two-term defect identity, its sharp constant, and equality structure.
An equivalent identity may exist in older triangle-geometry literature not exhaustively searchable in full text.
The 2016 Mathematics Magazine article was available only through metadata and abstract in the inspected lawful sources.
title: Exact defect decomposition for the Lemoine pedal-triangle minimum
